I made this guide while learning DSP because I kept losing the thread between one successful build and the next. It's meant to stay open {{strong_1}}while you're playing{{end_strong_1}}, not be read once from top to bottom and memorized.

Cube names used in this guide
DSP gives every cube a formal name, but colors are much easier to spot in the middle of a build. That's what we'll normally call them:
When a formal Matrix name appears later, it means the {{strong_1}}technology you click in the tech tree{{end_strong_1}}. Manufactured items, rates, stockpiles, and recipes stick to cube colors.

The route above is the simplest way through the game, not the only worthwhile project. It uses a Solar Sail swarm to reach photon production and white science. Build a permanent Sphere when you want something lasting; you can finish the route without one.
If you're playing with Dark Fog, RED gets your first planet defended and one local base cleared. That's enough combat for now; the rest can stay in the fog.
A few useful side projects will turn up along the way. Ignore them until one solves the problem in front of you; that's when it earns an introduction.
How to use this guide without constantly rereading it

{{strong_1}}Lost after a long play session?{{end_strong_1}} Use the colored strip on the right, jump to the part of the route you're working on, and let {{strong_2}}YOU ARE HERE{{end_strong_2}} do the remembering. That's what it's for.
The build cards use standard recipes, no rare-resource substitutions, and no proliferation unless an Operating Note says otherwise.

{{strong_1}}Card presentation:{{end_strong_1}} Cards are optional high-level production references. The guide tells you what matters and why; a card shows the complete shape of one useful line without turning its internals into a machine-count exercise.

{{strong_1}}Card grammar:{{end_strong_1}} {{strong_2}}Supplies{{end_strong_2}} names the raw or established inputs. {{strong_3}}Production Map{{end_strong_3}} shows short branches and their convergence in build order. {{strong_4}}Destination{{end_strong_4}} states the exact end-product target and where it goes. {{strong_5}}Surplus Yield{{end_strong_5}} names only real reusable or blocking byproduct types. {{strong_6}}Operating Note{{end_strong_6}} appears only when something changes how the line is built or kept running.

Finite batches, travel loadouts, research purchases, route configuration, and orbital operation remain in phase prose. Exact internal draw rates, machine counts, belt counts, fill timers, and capacity margins are intentionally left to the factory you actually build.

{{strong_1}}Buffer with a reason:{{end_strong_1}} mall products, expedition supplies, blocking byproducts, and deliberate phase batches benefit from visible limited storage. Giant buffers behind every line can hide a shortage until the whole factory fails at once; ordinary intermediates only need enough room to keep transport and production moving.

{{strong_1}}Storage limits use slots:{{end_strong_1}} The storage slider enables whole stack slots, not an exact item count. Card destinations state the number of enabled slots and the resulting maximum. If a target is smaller than one stack, pause the producing machine when the target is reached.
{{strong_1}}Need the next move? Follow the route.{{end_strong_1}} Need a whole production chain at a glance? Open its card. They start closed, and it's perfectly fine to leave them that way.

Your first proper phase has two jobs, and they belong together. Build a mall so basic supplies are waiting in boxes instead of wasting time replicating everything yourself. The mall already makes the blue cube ingredients so use the same growing factory to keep blue research running on its own. You need both before you move on.

Don’t wait until you can build everything at once. You can start each part of the mall as soon as you unlock its recipe. The first boxes will refill while blue research unlocks Thermal Power, Steel, and Foundation.
Don't get stuck in this phase for too long automating every recipe you have. You will have plenty of downtime waiting for tech completions to fill with busy work.

Run repeatable factory blocks east–west where possible and expect grid spacing to change as a build crosses latitude bands.
Save repeatable branches and station interfaces first. They adapt to real terrain and technology more gracefully than an early planet-sized stamp.

{{strong_1}}Bring power to the edge.{{end_strong_1}} Extend {{item_2201_1}} toward the planetary base and stop just outside its aggro range. If you pull aggro early, fall back and shoot down any chasing units, then make sure you have not left a {{item_2201_2}} inside aggro range.
